text:
There isn't one best combo, because it depends on how much power your RV uses. The pages I read gave specs but almost no prices for the bundles, so check current prices before you buy.

## Pick by RV type

**Weekend or van-style trips (fridge, lights, laptop, phone charging)**
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 with two SolarSaga 200W panels.** It has 1,070 Wh, 1,500 W output and 400 W max solar input. It weighs about 24 lb. Two 200W panels use the full 400 W input. [Buy the Explorer 1000 v2](https://amzn.to/463Djm2)
- **EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus.** It has 1,024 Wh, 1,800 W output and up to 1,000 W solar input, so it recharges faster. The article didn't name a panel brand, and it needs two separate panel connections to reach full input. [Buy the DELTA 3 Plus](https://amzn.to/45VmOIP)

**Full-time or off-grid use (bigger loads, maybe occasional AC)**
- **BLUETTI AC200L.** It has 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W output and up to 1,200 W solar input. It's heavy at about 62 lb and noisy, around 50 dBA at full load. It suits a semi-permanent setup with a folding or roof array. [Buy the AC200L](https://amzn.to/4qKjh9E)
- **Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro.** It has 3,024 Wh, 3,000 W output and up to 1,400 W solar input. It runs a 300 W fridge-plus-fan load for about 8.5 hours. [Search Amazon for the Explorer 3000 Pro](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=jackery+explorer+3000+pro&tag=ggref-20)

**Running a roof AC**
- **EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3.** It has 4,096 Wh, 4,000 W continuous output and 8,000 W surge, and you can expand it past 12 kWh. One article estimates about 2.3 hours on a 13,500 BTU roof AC. It's also quiet, under 30 dBA at low load. [Search Amazon for the DELTA Pro 3](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=ecoflow+delta+pro+3&tag=ggref-20)

**Best value I found: ALLPOWERS R4000**
- It has 3,456 Wh of LiFePO4 (3,500+ cycles), 3,600 W continuous and 6,000 W peak output, and an RV outlet. It accepts up to 2,000 W of solar across three inputs, but you need panels on all three to get that.
- Its store price is $1,499. Code **EXTRA12** brings that to **$1,319.12**. The code expires 11/15/2026 and the page's author confirmed it in the cart on 10/23.
- It weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb), so it should stay in the RV. It has a 5-year warranty. Returns take 30 days, you pay return shipping, and sale items may not be returnable.
- [Buy the ALLPOWERS R4000](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh). This is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you.

## Before you buy
- **Do the math first.** Add up your daily watt-hours. A fridge uses roughly 1–1.5 kWh a day, and a roof AC uses far more.
- **Match the panels to the station.** Check the station's voltage and current limits. Panel wattage over the input limit is wasted.
- **Plan on roughly 400–600 W of panels for a 2 kWh or larger battery.** Roof space is usually what limits you. Folding panels are flexible, but you have to set them up each time.
- **The sources are thin.** Two of the articles I read gave no prices. The comparison guides appear to earn affiliate commissions, and one of them used the same placeholder link for all three brands.

If you tell me your RV type, your main appliances (especially whether you run the AC), and your budget, I can narrow this to one station and the panel size to pair with it.
